concepts.name: Central Vigilance Commission, Enforcement Directorate and the National Commission for Minorities
concepts.description: The statutory basis, composition, appointment, tenure, organisation and working of the CVC; the structure, ranks, Director appointment and tenure, laws and functions of the Enforcement Directorate; and the composition, tenure, removal and civil-court powers of the National Commission for Minorities.
concepts.idea: The CVC, the ED and the NCM differ in legal basis, appointing committee, tenure and removal procedure, and UPSC tests these swaps and the minute rank, office and year details.
concepts.rule: The CVC began in 1964 by an executive resolution on the Santhanam Committee recommendation and became statutory through the CVC Act, 2003; it has a Central Vigilance Commissioner and up to two Vigilance Commissioners appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Prime Minister, the Union Home Minister and the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, for four years or age 65, and it supervises but does not itself have an investigating agency. The Enforcement Directorate (1956) is an executive agency under the Department of Revenue enforcing PMLA 2002, FEMA 1999 and the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act 2018, with the Director at New Delhi, Special Directors at five regional offices, Joint Directors at zonal offices and Deputy Directors at sub-zonal offices; its Director is picked by a committee headed by the Central Vigilance Commissioner, serves two years and may be extended a year at a time up to five years. The National Commission for Minorities is a statutory body under the Act of 1992 with a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and five Members nominated by the Centre (five including the Chairperson from minority communities) for three years; the Centre removes a member on six listed grounds, and the Commission has civil-court powers.
concepts.example: A search under PMLA is ordered by an ED zonal office headed by a Joint Director, while the officer who heads the headquarters in New Delhi is the Director of Enforcement, picked by a committee under the Central Vigilance Commissioner.

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes the legal position of the Enforcement Directorate?
questions.a: An executive agency under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, drawing its powers from statutes such as PMLA and FEMA
o: An executive agency under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, drawing its powers from statutes such as PMLA and FEMA
A statutory body created by the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 and placed under the administrative control of the Ministry of Home Affairs
A constitutional body whose Director can be removed from office only in the manner and on the grounds applicable to a Supreme Court judge
An attached office of the Central Vigilance Commission, which supervises and directs all of its investigations
questions.e: The ED is neither constitutional nor statutory; it is a law-enforcement agency under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, and enforces statutes such as PMLA and FEMA.
w: The Directorate is not created by PMLA and sits under the Finance Ministry's Department of Revenue, not the Home Ministry.
The ED has no constitutional status; it is neither a constitutional nor a statutory body.
The CVC does not supervise the ED; the ED works under the Department of Revenue.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Enforcement Directorate:

1. Under PMLA it may provisionally attach property and pursue confiscation through Adjudicating Authorities and Special Courts.
2. For contraventions of FEMA it imposes the monetary penalty itself, with no adjudicating authority involved.
3. It supports preventive detention in serious foreign-exchange and smuggling cases by sponsoring them under COFEPOSA.
4. Its powers of search, seizure and arrest under PMLA are open to judicial scrutiny.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: attachment and confiscation through Adjudicating Authorities and Special Courts are PMLA steps. Statement 2 is incorrect: under FEMA the ED investigates and assists adjudicating authorities in imposing penalties; it does not impose them itself. Statement 3 is correct: COFEPOSA sponsorship. Statement 4 is correct: these powers are subject to judicial scrutiny. So the correct combination is 1, 3 and 4 only.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct

Statement-II: A Member of the Commission may resign at any time by addressing the resignation to the Central Government.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a ground on which the Central Government may remove the Chairperson or a Member of the National Commission for Minorities before the end of the term?
questions.a: Absence from three consecutive meetings of the Commission without obtaining leave of absence
o: Absence from three consecutive meetings of the Commission without obtaining leave of absence
Engaging, during the term of office, in any paid employment outside the duties of the office
Acquiring a financial interest likely to affect the official functions prejudicially
Failure to submit the annual report of the Commission to the Centre within a year of the previous report
questions.e: The NCM list: insolvency, conviction with imprisonment for moral turpitude, unsound mind declared by a court, refusal or incapacity to act, absence from three consecutive meetings, and abuse of position detrimental to minorities or the public interest.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the functions of the Enforcement Directorate:

1. Under PMLA the ED itself tries accused persons and convicts them through its own adjudicating wing.
2. Under FEMA the ED investigates contraventions and capital-account violations and assists adjudicating authorities in imposing monetary penalties.
3. Under the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 the ED starts proceedings to declare fugitive economic offenders and to attach their property.
4. The ED sponsors cases for preventive detention under the National Security Act, 1980 in serious foreign-exchange and smuggling cases.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The ED investigates, attaches property, pursues confiscation through Adjudicating Authorities and Special Courts and files prosecution complaints; trial is by the courts. Statement 2 is correct: Under FEMA the ED investigates contraventions and capital-account violations and assists adjudicating authorities in imposing monetary penalties. Statement 3 is correct: Under the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 the ED starts proceedings to declare fugitive economic offenders and to attach their property. Statement 4 is incorrect: It sponsors such cases under COFEPOSA, not the National Security Act.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Minorities:

1. The Act of 1992 itself names the communities entitled to the Commission's protection.
2. A Member who wishes to resign writes to the Chief Justice of India.
3. The Constitution does not explicitly define 'minority'.
4. A report of the Commission that concerns a State is forwarded to that State Government, which lays it before the State legislature with a memorandum of action taken.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the Act does not name the communities; it lets the Central Government notify them (five in 1993, with the Jains added in 2014). Statement 2 is incorrect: the resignation is addressed to the Central Government. Statement 3 is correct: the Constitution does not explicitly define 'minority'. Statement 4 is correct. So exactly 2 statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: statements 3 and 4 are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: statements 1 and 2 are incorrect.
'All four' includes statements 1 and 2, which are incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the working of the Central Vigilance Commission:

1. It has no investigating agency of its own and works through the CBI and the departmental vigilance units.
2. It exercises superintendence over the CBI in respect of every offence that the CBI investigates.
3. A Central Government authority that declines to follow the Commission's advice must send a reasoned note, recorded in writing, to the Commission.
4. Its proceedings carry a judicial character because it enjoys the powers of a civil court.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The CVC has no investigating machinery of its own; it is largely advisory and supervisory, working through the CBI and the departmental vigilance units. Statement 2 is incorrect: Its superintendence over the Delhi Special Police Establishment is limited to the investigation of offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988. Statement 3 is correct: When a Central Government authority does not agree with the CVC's advice it must communicate its reasons, recorded in writing, to the Commission. Statement 4 is correct: The CVC has all the powers of a civil court and its proceedings have a judicial character.

questions.q: The Enforcement Directorate traces its origin to an 'Enforcement Unit' created to deal with exchange-control violations. In which year was that unit established?

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the tenure of the Director of Enforcement:

1. For the ED, the base term laid down in the CVC Act, 2003 is two years.
2. The extension of the tenure beyond two years was enabled by the Delhi Special Police Establishment (Amendment) Act, 2021.
3. The total tenure, including the initial two years, can go up to five years.
4. Extension is granted one year at a time, so at most three annual extensions are possible.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: For the ED, the base term laid down in the CVC Act, 2003 is two years. Statement 2 is incorrect: For the ED the extension was enabled by the Central Vigilance Commission (Amendment) Act, 2021; the DSPE amendment of 2021 relates to the CBI Director. Statement 3 is correct: The total tenure, including the initial two years, can go up to five years. Statement 4 is correct: Extension is granted one year at a time, so three annual extensions after the initial two years reach the five-year ceiling. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q: Which one of the following statutes is among the laws that the Enforcement Directorate is entrusted to enforce?

The Customs Act is administered by the customs authorities, not the ED.

concepts.name: National Commission for Minorities factsheet and the Central Information Commission under the RTI Act
concepts.description: The functions, history and notified communities of the National Commission for Minorities, and the nature, 2019 amendment, composition, appointment, tenure, removal, powers and civil-court powers of the Central Information Commission, with the debates and challenges around the RTI Act.
concepts.idea: The Central Information Commission is a statutory body whose tenure and service conditions were shifted to the Centre in 2019, and UPSC tests who appoints, who removes, what powers it has and how the NCM factsheet differs.
concepts.rule: The NCM nine-point mandate is evaluative, monitoring and recommendatory; a Minorities Commission was set up in 1978, became statutory under the 1992 Act, the first statutory Commission was constituted in 1993 and Jains were added to the five notified communities in 2014. The Central Information Commission is an independent statutory body under the RTI Act, 2005 with a Chief Information Commissioner and up to ten Information Commissioners appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister. Since the RTI (Amendment) Act, 2019 their term and service conditions are prescribed by the Central Government, where earlier the term was five years or age 65 and the status matched the Election Commissioners; they are not reappointed, and the President removes them on listed grounds or after a Supreme Court inquiry for misbehaviour or incapacity. The Commission decides second appeals and complaints, has civil-court powers under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and can penalise a Public Information Officer at Rs 250 a day up to Rs 25,000; Section 22 gives the Act overriding effect over the Official Secrets Act.
concepts.example: A citizen refused information by a Central Government PSU files a second appeal with the CIC, which can summon the officer, inspect the record and impose a penalty of Rs 250 for each day of delay up to Rs 25,000.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Right to Information Act, 2005 overrides the Official Secrets Act, 1923 where the two are inconsistent.
Statement-II: Section 8(2) of the RTI Act bars disclosure of information protected by the Official Secrets Act even where the public interest in disclosure outweighs the harm.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: Section 22 gives the RTI Act overriding effect. Statement-II is incorrect: Section 8(2) permits disclosure, even of material covered by the Official Secrets Act, when public interest outweighs the harm. Statement-II reverses Section 8(2), so it is incorrect.
w: Statement-II is incorrect, so it cannot explain Statement-I.

concepts.name: State Information Commission: composition, tenure, removal and powers
concepts.description: The State Information Commission under the RTI Act, 2005: composition and appointment by the Governor, eligibility, tenure and service conditions after the 2019 amendment, removal, complaint jurisdiction, civil-court and inquiry powers, powers to secure compliance, and the reform suggestions for the Information Commissions.
concepts.idea: The State Information Commission mirrors the Central Commission but with the Governor as appointing and removing authority and a Chief Minister-led committee, and UPSC tests those swaps and the long list of its powers.
concepts.rule: The State Information Commission is a statutory body under Section 15 of the RTI Act, 2005 with a State Chief Information Commissioner and not more than ten State Information Commissioners, appointed by the Governor on the recommendation of the Chief Minister, the Leader of Opposition in the Legislative Assembly and a State Cabinet Minister nominated by the Chief Minister. Members must be eminent persons and cannot be Members of Parliament or of any legislature, hold an office of profit, belong to a political party or carry on business or a profession; since 2019 their term (age 65 at most), salary and service conditions are prescribed by the Central Government and cannot be varied to their disadvantage during service. The Governor removes a member on insolvency, moral turpitude, paid employment, infirmity or a prejudicial interest, and for proved misbehaviour or incapacity only after the Supreme Court upholds the charge on a reference. The Commission receives complaints on six heads, can act suo motu, has civil-court powers under the Code of Civil Procedure, may examine any record, can direct compliance, compensation and penalties, and reports annually to the State Government, which places the report before the State Legislature.
concepts.example: If a State department has not appointed a Public Information Officer, an applicant complains to the State Information Commission, which can direct the department to appoint one and, in an inquiry, can examine any record of the department.

concepts.name: State Information Commission summary and the National Commission for Women
concepts.description: The summary of the State Information Commission, and the origin, composition, term, removal, functions, civil-court powers and working of the National Commission for Women under the NCW Act, 1990.
concepts.idea: The NCW is a statutory, autonomous body whose members the Centre nominates and removes on six listed grounds, and its powers are investigative and recommendatory rather than punitive.
concepts.rule: The State Information Commission is the statutory State counterpart of the CIC, with a State Chief Information Commissioner and up to ten State Information Commissioners appointed by the Governor on the recommendation of the Chief Minister, the Leader of Opposition and a State Cabinet Minister. The NCW was constituted on 31 January 1992 under the NCW Act, 1990 as an autonomous statutory body, with a Chairperson, five Members (at least one each from the SCs and STs) and a Member-Secretary, all nominated by the Central Government for three years. The Centre removes a member who is insolvent, convicted with imprisonment for moral turpitude, of unsound mind, refuses or is incapable of acting, absent from three consecutive meetings or abuses position. Its fourteen functions include investigating safeguards, reviewing laws, taking suo motu notice, inspecting places of custody and funding litigation; it has civil-court powers while investigating but its findings are advisory, and the Parivarik Mahila Lok Adalat is its family-dispute forum.
concepts.example: The NCW takes suo motu notice of a dowry-harassment case and summons the police officers concerned, but it can only recommend action to the authorities and cannot itself convict the accused.

concepts.idea: The NCW investigates and recommends without adjudicating, while NITI Aayog is an extra-constitutional, non-statutory think tank whose composition, ranks and hubs are the minute facts UPSC tests.
concepts.rule: The NCW takes complaints orally, in writing, online or suo motu on domestic violence, sexual violence, trafficking, dowry harassment, honour-based crimes and discrimination, seeks reports from the police and officials, recommends FIRs, disciplinary action and compensation, and refers cases to courts, legal aid bodies and Parivarik Mahila Lok Adalats, but it does not adjudicate. NITI Aayog was set up on 1 January 2015 by an executive resolution of the Union Cabinet in place of the Planning Commission; it is neither constitutional nor statutory. Its Chairperson is the Prime Minister; the Governing Council has the Chief Ministers of all States, of Union Territories with legislatures and the Lieutenant Governors of the others; Regional Councils are temporary, issue-based bodies chaired by the Chairperson or nominee; the Vice-Chairperson has Cabinet rank, Full-time Members the rank of Minister of State, there are at most two Part-time and four Ex-officio Members, and the CEO is of Secretary rank. Its work is organised in the Team India Hub and the Knowledge and Innovation Hub.

concepts.rule: NILERD (formerly the Institute of Applied Manpower Research, 1962) is an autonomous organisation under NITI Aayog and the DMEO (2015, by merging the PEO and the IEO) is an attached office. NITI Aayog follows seven principles (Antyodaya, inclusion, village, demographic dividend, people participation, governance, sustainability) and seven pillars, and unlike the Planning Commission of 1950 it cannot allocate plan funds. In the comparison: the NHRC and SHRC have three years or age 70, the Lokpal five years or age 70, the CVC four years or age 65, the CBI (1963) is non-statutory with a Director chosen by the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition and the Chief Justice of India or nominee, the Lokpal committee has five members, the NHRC committee six, the CVC committee is the Prime Minister, Home Minister and Leader of Opposition, and the ED Director is chosen by a committee under the Central Vigilance Commissioner. Chronology: ED 1956, CBI 1963, CVC 1964 (statutory 2003), NCW Act 1990, NCM Act 1992, NHRC Act 1993, RTI Act 2005, Lokpal Act 2013, NITI Aayog 2015.
concepts.example: An aspirant asked who recommends the Lokpal Chairperson must say a five-member committee including the Speaker and an eminent jurist, not the three-member committee that recommends the CBI Director.

NILERD is an attached office of NITI Aayog, while the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office is a central autonomous organisation of the Government

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the selection committees for the appointment of heads and members of bodies:

1. The National Human Rights Commission's committee is the Prime Minister, the Union Home Minister and the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha.
2. The State Human Rights Commission's committee includes the Chief Minister, the Speaker of the Assembly, the State Home Minister and the Leader of Opposition in the Assembly.
3. The Information Commissions and the National Human Rights Commission use the same committee of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition and a Union Cabinet Minister.
4. The CBI Director is selected by a panel made up of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and either the Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court judge he nominates.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: That is the Central Vigilance Commission's committee; the NHRC's is a six-member committee of the Prime Minister, the Speaker, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, the Leaders of Opposition in both Houses and the Home Minister. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: That committee is correct for the Central Information Commission only. Statement 4 is correct: The CBI Director is selected by a panel made up of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and either the Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court judge he nominates.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 4, which is correct.
'2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office:

1. It was established in 2015 as an attached office of NITI Aayog by merging the Programme Evaluation Organisation and the Independent Evaluation Office.
2. It is an autonomous body like NILERD, with its own governing board.
3. It conducts independent evaluations of flagship and sectoral programmes and helps Ministries design evaluation Terms of Reference while tracking SDG progress.
4. It also fosters cooperative federalism by engaging States in monitoring and evaluation and strengthens feedback loops for policy correction.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: it was established in 2015 as an attached office of NITI Aayog by merging the Programme Evaluation Organisation and the Independent Evaluation Office. Statement 2 is incorrect: it is an attached office; NILERD is the autonomous body. Statement 3 is correct: it conducts independent evaluations of flagship and sectoral programmes and helps Ministries design evaluation Terms of Reference while tracking SDG progress. Statement 4 is correct: it fosters cooperative federalism by engaging States in monitoring and evaluation and strengthens feedback loops for policy correction.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: the office does engage States in monitoring.
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: it is an attached office, not an autonomous body.
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: it was set up in 2015 by merging the two evaluation bodies.

questions.q: The activities of NITI Aayog are divided between two hubs. Which one of the following correctly describes the Team India Hub?
questions.a: It fosters cooperative federalism, designs policy and programme frameworks and coordinates the Commission's engagement with the States
o: It fosters cooperative federalism, designs policy and programme frameworks and coordinates the Commission's engagement with the States
It maintains a resource centre and a repository of best practices and builds partnerships with universities, think tanks and non-governmental organisations
It conducts independent evaluations of flagship programmes and helps Ministries frame the terms of reference for evaluation studies

questions.e: NITI Aayog's work is divided into the Team India Hub, which carries out the mandate of fostering cooperative federalism and designing policy and programme frameworks and coordinates engagement with States, and the Knowledge and Innovation Hub, which keeps the resource centre and repository of best practices and builds partnerships.
w: That is the description of the Knowledge and Innovation Hub, the other hub.
Independent programme evaluation is the work of the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office, not a hub.
NITI Aayog has no power to allocate plan funds to the States.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Unlike the erstwhile Planning Commission, NITI Aayog does not allocate plan funds to the States.
Statement-II: NITI Aayog was set up in place of the Planning Commission as a policy think tank that gives directional and strategic input to governments, rather than as a body that controls resources.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: NITI Aayog has no power to allocate plan funds. Statement-II is correct: it replaced the Planning Commission as the premier policy think tank of the Government, offering directional and strategic input. A body whose mandate is advisory input and not control of resources is a body with no fund-allocation power, so II explains I.
w: Statement-II is the reason behind Statement-I, since an advisory think tank has no fund-allocation power, so 'does not explain' is wrong.
Statement-II is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect: NITI Aayog is the Government's premier policy think tank.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about NITI Aayog and related bodies:

1. Antyodaya as a guiding principle of NITI Aayog is tied to Mahatma Gandhi's idea.
2. NITI Aayog is composed of the Prime Minister as Chairperson, the Governing Council, a Vice-Chairperson, Full-time, Part-time and Ex-officio Members and a Chief Executive Officer.
3. NITI Aayog follows five guiding principles of governance.
4. NILERD is funded mainly by grants-in-aid from the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: NITI Aayog ties Antyodaya to Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay's idea, not Mahatma Gandhi's. Statement 2 is correct: NITI Aayog is composed of the Prime Minister as Chairperson, the Governing Council, a Vice-Chairperson, Full-time, Part-time and Ex-officio Members and a Chief Executive Officer. Statement 3 is incorrect: it is guided by seven principles, not five. Statement 4 is incorrect: NILERD is funded mainly by grants-in-aid from NITI Aayog, not the Ministry of Labour and Employment. So exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements is correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements is correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the appointment of heads of bodies:

1. The Chairperson and Members of the NCW and the NCM are nominated by the Central Government, without a statutory selection committee.
2. The Director of Enforcement is chosen by the Central Government on service rules without any committee.
3. The Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission is appointed on the recommendation of a committee headed by the Chief Justice of India.
4. The Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog is appointed by the Prime Minister and enjoys the rank of a Cabinet Minister.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the NCW and NCM heads are nominated by the Central Government with no statutory selection committee. Statement 2 is incorrect: the ED Director is appointed on the recommendation of a committee headed by the Central Vigilance Commissioner. Statement 3 is incorrect: the NHRC committee is headed by the Prime Minister, not the Chief Justice of India. Statement 4 is correct: the Vice-Chairperson is appointed by the Prime Minister and has Cabinet rank. So exactly 2 statements are correct.
w: 'Only three' counts statement 2 or 3, both of which are incorrect.
'All four' includes statements 2 and 3, which are incorrect.
'Only one' misses one of statements 1 and 4, which are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the establishment of bodies:

1. The CBI is a statutory body because its powers derive from the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946.
2. The CBI was created in 1963 by a resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs.
3. The Central and State Information Commissions were set up under the RTI Act after the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act of 2013.
4. The National Commission for Women Act (1990) came before the National Commission for Minorities Act (1992).

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It was created by a 1963 resolution and is not a statutory body, even though its powers come from the 1946 Act. Statement 2 is correct: The CBI was created in 1963 by a resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs. Statement 3 is incorrect: The RTI Act is of 2005, earlier than the Lokpal Act of 2013. Statement 4 is correct. So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the guiding principles of NITI Aayog:

1. Antyodaya: uplift of the poor and marginalised so that benefits reach the last mile; it is tied to Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay's idea.
2. Inclusion: redress inequalities of gender, caste, religion, region and economic class.
3. People's Participation: a State-driven development process in which citizens are treated as beneficiaries.
4. Village: integrate villages institutionally, with bottom-up planning through local institutions.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Antyodaya is tied to Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay's idea of uplifting the last person. Statement 2 is correct: Inclusion means redressing inequalities of gender, caste, religion, region and economic class. Statement 3 is incorrect: it means a people-driven process with active citizen involvement. Statement 4 is correct: Village means integrating villages institutionally, with bottom-up planning through local institutions.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: Antyodaya is tied to Deendayal Upadhyay's idea.
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: participation is people-driven, not State-driven.
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: Inclusion covers gender, caste, religion, region and class.
